## 2026-11-01 17:14 · claude-macbook · mc-motion

Owner design rule (2026-11-01): vanilla silhouette first.
- Never split the 6 boxes: no elbows or knees.
- Avoid realistic RPG-style motion (Better Combat, Epic Fight); it breaks the vanilla feel.
- Rig: 12 joints. Each box rides a joint at its vanilla pivot, hung from a boxless connector 1-2 px inside the torso:
  - chest 1 px above pelvis
  - neck (0,2,0) -> head
  - clavicle (±3,2,0) -> arm
  - hip (±1.9,10,0) -> leg
- Liveliness comes from small pivot motion. Target reaction: "only 6 vanilla boxes, why does it look more alive?"
- The split rig (M0 v1) worked for items, armor, cape and mannequins.
- Known issue from the split rig: the outer 3D skin layer on lower limbs followed the upper box. Moot now; fix if splitting ever returns.

## 2026-11-01 16:16 · claude-macbook · mc-motion

Direction (pending owner decisions): drop EMF as runtime. Own Fabric mod: pure-Java core (no MC imports) plus a thin 26.1 adapter. Ecosystem formats are rig, style and intent JSON. Doc: /Volumes/SangHun/dev/mc/research/direction.md
Hook points verified in the 26.1.2 jar:
- AvatarRenderer.extractRenderState(Avatar, AvatarRenderState, float)
- PlayerModel.setupAnim(AvatarRenderState)
- PlayerModel.createMesh(CubeDeformation, boolean)
- PlayerModel.translateToHand (single choke point for held items)
- HumanoidArmorLayer.getArmorModel
- SubmitNodeCollector$CustomGeometryRenderer
- Fabric API FabricRenderState + RenderStateDataKey (fabric-rendering-v1 in 0.155.3)
Avatar covers Player and Mannequin, so mannequins can test the remote-player path. Intermediate joints live only in the solver skeleton; render keeps the 6 top-level parts plus 4 child parts.
